title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
read_level: full (v2 PDF, 4-page short paper incl. tables; no appendix present)
metadata_mismatch: none (read v2 dated 14 Nov 2026; first version date taken from metadata)
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra (and separately DeepSeek) write reusable update programs that turn accumulated experimental measurements into direct corrections of a restricted set of native parameters of pretrained scientific predictors, validated and saved back into the checkpoint.
domain: scientific predictors: CRISPRi cell responses (GEARS), earthquake P-wave picking (PhaseNet), weather Z500 (ClimaX), shallow-water PDE (FNO2d), gene recommendation MLPs, RNA decoders (scGPT, scFoundation+GEARS)
editor: GPT-6 Astra (interactive coding session) and DeepSeek (deepseek-flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 via API); LLMs write the update program, which then runs numerically (regularized least squares / L-BFGS) each round
target: GEARS, PhaseNet, ClimaX, FNO2d, MLP recommenders, scGPT, scF+GEARS; editable pools of 1,024/27/192/129 parameters for the four prediction tasks; total model sizes not stated except 244 edited = 0.0068% for HepG2 MLP
interface: code/tensor tools (LLM-written update program computing closed-form/regularized corrections)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (per-round fit, validate on held-out feedback folds, accept/reject, then select next experimental batch)
self_editing: no; the LLM edits separate scientific predictors
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "Including 128 hidden biases, the 244 edited parameters account for 0.0068% of the model" (Fig. 1, HepG2); "final counts are 1,024 for GEARS, 26 for PhaseNet, four for ClimaX and 129 for FNO2d" (Sec. 3.2)

headline_results.claim: Lower primary error than Adam on identical feedback and writable params across 4 predictors
headline_results.quote: relative improvements range from 5.10% for FNO2d to 18.56% for PhaseNet
For weather prediction, changing four output-bias parameters reduces root mean squared error by 13.28%.

headline_results.claim: Functional recommendation BU improves e.g. HepG2 B=20

headline_results.quote: GPT-6 Astra editing improves mean utility by 8.30%, 14.97% and 303.43% for LC3, NBR1 and HuH7
mean MSE reductions of 1.85% for scGPT and 7.49% for scF+GEARS relative to their adapted checkpoints

baselines_and_controls: Adam fitting the same 12 objectives on identical feedback, writable coordinates, validation folds and acceptance rules (prediction tasks, RNA calibration); initial unedited MLP (recommendation, discovery); adapted checkpoint (RNA). No random-edit or no-LLM-program control reported.
runs_and_variance: Prediction tasks: single execution seed ("The four tasks use execution seed17"), no variance. Recommendation/discovery/RNA: "Mean ± sample SD across three training seeds after averaging five gene folds per seed" (Table 2).
robustness_of_edits: not tested beyond save/reload: "Native checkpoint reload reproduces the accepted predictions" (Sec. 3.2)
verification: none formal; statistical acceptance gate: accept when "validation loss improves by at least 0.1% over the initial model and loss on observed history worsens by no more than 5%" (Sec. 3.1)
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a; note the LLM writes the program once and the numeric correction is computed by regularized least squares/L-BFGS, so the per-round numeric edit is not LLM-generated
limitations_stated: No explicit limitations section. Notes FNO2d published split "includes training-equivalent initial states"; Ethics notes "Original checkpoints are retained so updates remain reversible."
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog)
notes_for_survey: Closed-loop WSP for active experimentation: LLM-authored update programs, numeric corrections via ridge/L-BFGS over tiny editable pools, accept/reject on feedback folds. The Adam baseline is matched on parameters and feedback; prediction-task results are single-seed. The LLM role is program construction, not per-weight value writing.
